questions.question: Galvanisation protects iron from rusting by coating it with a thin layer of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc metal only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a metallurgical process used to protect **Iron** and **Steel** from **Rusting** by applying a thin, protective coating of **Zinc**.
 
• The process is highly effective because **Zinc** acts as a physical barrier between the metal and the atmosphere, preventing **Oxygen** and **Moisture** from reaching the surface of the **Iron**.
 
• The most common method utilized in industries is **Hot-dip galvanizing**, where the metal components are submerged in a bath of molten **Zinc** at temperatures typically around **450 degrees Celsius** (**842 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• A unique feature of this process is **Sacrificial Protection**; since **Zinc** is more chemically active (electropositive) than **Iron**, it corrodes in preference to the **Iron**, even if the coating is scratched or damaged.
 
• While other metals like **Nickel**, **Chromium**, or **Tin** can be used for coating (in processes like electroplating), the specific term **Galvanisation** refers exclusively to the application of **Zinc**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rusting of Iron**: 
 
 
• **Rusting** is an oxidation reaction that occurs when **Iron** reacts with **Oxygen** in the presence of **Water** or **Moisture**.
 
• The chemical formula for rust is **Fe2O3.nH2O**, which is known as **Hydrated Iron(III) Oxide**. It is a reddish-brown flaky substance that weakens the structural integrity of the metal.
 
 
 
• **Other Methods of Rust Prevention**:
 
 
• **Painting and Greasing**: Provides a simple barrier to block **Air** and **Water**.
 
• **Alloying**: Mixing **Iron** with elements like **Chromium** (at least **10.5%**) and **Nickel** produces **Stainless Steel**, which is highly resistant to corrosion.
 
• **Anodizing**: Primarily used for **Aluminium**, it thickens the natural oxide layer on the metal surface.
 
• **Tinning**: Coating **Iron** or **Steel** with **Tin**, often used for food containers as **Tin** is non-toxic.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options**:
 
 
• **Silver**: It is an expensive precious metal and would be economically unviable for industrial rust protection.
 
• **Copper**: If used as a coating, it can actually accelerate the corrosion of **Iron** if the coating is breached because **Iron** is more reactive than **Copper**.
 
• **Nickel**: Used in **Electroplating** to provide a shiny finish and corrosion resistance, but it does not provide the same sacrificial protection as **Zinc**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **Galvanisation** is named after the **Italian** scientist **Luigi Galvani**, who studied the effects of electricity on biological tissues, though the industrial coating process was developed later in the **19th Century**.
 
• In a **Galvanic Cell** setup, the **Zinc** acts as the **Anode** and the **Iron** acts as the **Cathode**, ensuring the base metal remains protected as long as the **Zinc** is present.
 
• Common applications of galvanized **Iron** include **Roofing sheets**, **Water pipes**, **Fencing**, and **Automotive body parts**.
</ul

questions.question: When a person stands stationary on the ground, the force of gravity exerted by the Earth on the person (Action) and the normal force exerted by the ground on the person (Reaction) are equal and opposite. Is this an action-reaction pair, according to Newton's Third Law?

options.text: Yes, because they balance each other, preventing motion.
No, because the two forces act on different objects.
Yes, because the two forces are equal and opposite in magnitude.
No, because the two forces act on the same object.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No, because the two forces act on the same object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Third Law of Motion** states that for every action, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**. A fundamental criterion for these forces to be considered an **action-reaction pair** is that they must act on **two different objects**.
 
• In the given scenario, the **force of gravity** (the Earth pulling the person downward) and the **normal force** (the ground pushing the person upward) both act on the **same object**—the person.
 
• Because both forces are applied to the **person**, they cannot constitute an action-reaction pair according to the **Third Law**. Instead, they represent a state of **static equilibrium**. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• Statement 1 suggests they are a pair because they balance each other. However, **balancing forces** that prevent motion are related to **Newton's First Law** (equilibrium) and specifically act on a single body, which contradicts the definition of a Third Law pair. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Statement 2 is factually incorrect in its premise regarding the specific forces mentioned; the gravity and normal force in this example are both exerted **on the person**, not on different objects. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Statement 3 claims they are a pair simply because they are **equal and opposite**. While action-reaction pairs are indeed equal and opposite, not all equal and opposite forces are action-reaction pairs. They must also act on different bodies and be of the same **physical nature**. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Identifying True Action-Reaction Pairs**:
 
 
• The reaction to the **Earth's gravitational pull** on the person is the **person's gravitational pull** on the **Earth**. These two forces act on different bodies (Person and Earth).
 
• The reaction to the **ground pushing up** on the person (Normal Force) is the **person pushing down** on the **ground**. These two forces act on different bodies (Person and Ground).
 
 
 
• **Nature of Forces**: Action-reaction pairs must be of the **same nature**. Gravity is a **field force** (non-contact), whereas the normal force is a **contact force** (electromagnetic in origin at the atomic level). A field force and a contact force can never form a **Newtonian pair**.
 
• **Equilibrium vs. Third Law**:
 
 
• **Equilibrium** involves multiple forces acting on **one object** that sum to a **net force of zero**, resulting in zero **acceleration**.
 
• **Newton's Third Law** describes a symmetry in nature where forces always occur in pairs acting on **interacting objects**. These forces never cancel each other out because they act on **different systems**.
 
 
 
• **Simultaneity**: In an action-reaction pair, there is no **time delay**. The action does not "cause" the reaction after a lapse of time; both forces appear and disappear **simultaneously**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mathematical Representation**: Newton's Third Law is often expressed as **FAB = -FBA**, where **FAB** is the force exerted by object A on object B, and **FBA** is the force exerted by object B on object A.
 
• **Independence of Motion**: The **Third Law** holds true whether the objects are **stationary**, moving at a **constant velocity**, or **accelerating**.
 
• **Common Examples**:
 
 
• **Recoil of a Gun**: The gun exerts a forward force on the **bullet** (action), and the bullet exerts an equal backward force on the **gun** (reaction).
 
• **Swimming**: A swimmer pushes the **water** backward (action), and the water pushes the **swimmer** forward (reaction).
 
• **Walking**: A person pushes the **ground** backward with their feet (action), and the ground pushes the **person** forward (reaction).
 
 
 
• **Mass Influence**: Although the forces are equal in **magnitude**, the resulting **accelerations** can be vastly different depending on the **mass** of the objects (**a = F/m**). This is why we don't see the Earth move when we jump, even though we pull on it with the same force it pulls on us.

questions.question: Why does the blue colour of copper sulphate solution fade when an iron nail is dipped in it?

options.text: Copper sulphate is converted into iron sulphate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper sulphate is converted into iron sulphate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **iron nail** is placed in a **copper sulphate (CuSO4)** solution, a **single displacement reaction** takes place. In this process, **iron**, being a more reactive metal, displaces **copper** from its salt solution.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: **Fe (s) + CuSO4 (aq) -> FeSO4 (aq) + Cu (s)**. This shows that **copper sulphate** is converted into **iron (II) sulphate** (also known as **ferrous sulphate**). ***Hence, the statement that copper sulphate is converted into iron sulphate is correct.***
 
• The **blue colour** of the **copper sulphate** solution is due to the presence of **Cu2+ ions**. As the reaction proceeds, the concentration of these ions decreases, causing the **blue colour to fade** and eventually turn **light green**.
 
• **Iron sulphate (FeSO4)**, which is formed in the solution, imparts a **light green colour** to the liquid. ***Hence, the statement that iron sulphate is colourless is incorrect.***
 
• The displaced **copper metal** does not dissolve; instead, it settles on the surface of the **iron nail** as a **reddish-brown** coating. ***Hence, the statement that copper dissolves in water is incorrect.***
 
• This reaction is not a decomposition; it is a **redox reaction** where **iron** is oxidized and **copper** is reduced. ***Hence, the statement that copper sulphate decomposes is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:** This is a list of metals arranged in the order of their decreasing chemical reactivity. In this series, **Iron (Fe)** is placed above **Copper (Cu)**, which explains why iron can displace copper from its compounds.
 
• **Copper Sulphate (CuSO4):** Often called **Blue Vitriol**, it typically exists as a pentahydrate (**CuSO4.5H2O**). It is widely used in **agriculture** as a fungicide and in **educational laboratories** to demonstrate displacement reactions.
 
• **Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4):** Known as **Green Vitriol**, it is used industrially in the manufacture of **inks** and as a **reducing agent** in chemical processes. In medicine, it is used to treat **iron deficiency anemia**.
 
• **Redox Reactions:** In the given reaction, **Iron** loses two electrons (**oxidation**) to become **Fe2+**, while the **Copper** ions gain two electrons (**reduction**) to become solid **Copper**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Visual Observations:** During this experiment, two distinct changes are observed: the **blue colour** of the solution changes to **light green**, and the **greyish iron nail** acquires a **brownish** texture.
 
• **Duration:** Usually, the fading of the blue colour is observable within **20 to 30 minutes** of immersion, depending on the **molarity** (concentration) of the solution.
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:** The total mass of the reactants (**Iron + Copper Sulphate**) remains equal to the total mass of the products (**Ferrous Sulphate + Copper**) in a closed system.
</ul

questions.question: Under what spatial condition is the magnitude of the force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a uniform magnetic field observed to be the highest?

options.text: When the current and field are parallel.
When the current is varied instantaneously.
When the current flows towards the south pole of the magnet.
When the current and field are perpendicular to each other.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When the current and field are perpendicular to each other**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnitude of the **magnetic force** acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a **uniform magnetic field** is determined by the formula **F = BIL sin θ**, where **F** is the force, **B** is the magnetic field strength, **I** is the current, **L** is the length of the conductor, and **θ** is the angle between the conductor and the field.
 
• The force is observed to be the **highest** (maximum) when the angle **θ** is **90 degrees**. This occurs because the value of **sin 90°** is **1**, which is the maximum possible value for the sine function. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• When the current and the magnetic field are **parallel** or **anti-parallel** to each other, the angle **θ** is **0 degrees** or **180 degrees**. Since **sin 0°** and **sin 180°** are both **0**, the magnetic force acting on the conductor is **zero**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Varying the current **instantaneously** may change the magnitude of the force over time, but it does not represent the **spatial condition** (alignment) required for the maximum force to be exerted at any given moment. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The direction of current flowing towards a specific pole (like the **south pole**) does not inherently define the angle **θ** unless the orientation of the magnetic field lines relative to that pole is specified as being **perpendicular**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnetic Flux Density (B):** It represents the strength of the **magnetic field**. The **SI unit** for magnetic flux density is the **Tesla (T)**. One Tesla is defined as **one Newton** of force per **Ampere-meter**.
 
• **Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule:** This rule is used to determine the direction of the **mechanical force** exerted on a conductor. If the **forefinger** points in the direction of the **magnetic field** and the **middle finger** points in the direction of the **current**, then the **thumb** represents the direction of the **force** (motion).
 
• **Lorentz Force:** While the formula **F = BIL sin θ** applies to conductors, the fundamental force on a single **moving charge (q)** with **velocity (v)** in a magnetic field is **F = qvB sin θ**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Force:** The force is directly proportional to the **magnitude of current (I)**, the **length of the conductor (L)**, and the **strength of the magnetic field (B)**. If any of these values increase, the force acting on the conductor also increases proportionally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vector Representation:** The force is mathematically expressed as a **vector product** (cross product): **F = I (L × B)**. This implies that the resulting force is always **perpendicular** to both the direction of the current and the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• **Applications:** This principle is the foundational mechanism behind the operation of **electric motors**, **galvanometers**, and **loudspeakers**, where electrical energy is converted into mechanical work via magnetic interaction.
 
• **Maximum Condition:** In most practical motor designs, the armature is configured to ensure the **current-carrying wires** move **perpendicular** to the **magnetic field** as much as possible to maintain **peak torque** and efficiency.

questions.question: What is a necessary property of the electrolyte used during the refining of metals by electrolysis?

options.text: It must be an aqueous or molten solution of a suitable metal salt
It must remain completely non-reactive throughout the procedure
It must efficiently conduct heat during the electrochemical process
It must be composed of both water and a layer of neutral oil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It must be an aqueous or molten solution of a suitable metal salt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of **electrolytic refining** is used to obtain highly **pure metals** from impure samples. In this process, the **electrolyte** must be a medium that allows the movement of metal ions between the electrodes.
 
• A necessary property of the electrolyte is that it must be an **aqueous or molten solution of a suitable metal salt**. This ensures that the electrolyte contains the same metal ions as the metal being purified, facilitating the transfer of pure metal to the cathode. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The electrolyte cannot remain completely **non-reactive**. In fact, it must actively participate in the **ion exchange** process, where metal ions from the solution are reduced at the cathode and metal atoms from the anode are oxidized into the solution. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• While **electrolysis** may generate heat due to resistance (Joule heating), the primary required property is **ionic conductivity** (the ability to conduct electricity via ions), not specifically the efficiency of conducting heat. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The electrolyte must be a **homogeneous conductive medium**. Using a layer of **neutral oil** would act as an **insulator** and prevent the flow of electric current, thus halting the refining process. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Electrolytic Refining:**
 
 
• It is a technique used for the extraction and purification of metals like **Copper (Cu)**, **Zinc (Zn)**, **Tin (Sn)**, **Nickel (Ni)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**.
 
• In this setup, a thick block of the **impure metal** is made the **anode** (positive electrode), and a thin strip of **pure metal** is made the **cathode** (negative electrode).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Electrolyte:**
 
 
• The electrolyte is typically a **water-soluble salt** of the metal being refined. For example, in copper refining, **acidified Copper Sulphate (CuSO4)** is used.
 
• When **electric current** is passed through the electrolyte, the impure metal from the anode dissolves into the electrolyte as **cations**.
 
• An equivalent amount of pure metal ions from the electrolyte are then deposited onto the cathode.
 
 
 
• **Fate of Impurities:**
 
 
• **Soluble impurities** go into the solution during the process.
 
• **Insoluble impurities** settle down at the bottom of the anode and are known as **anode mud**. This mud often contains precious metals like **Gold** and **Silver**, which can be recovered later.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Equations:**
 
 
• At the **Anode (Oxidation)**: M → Mⁿ⁺ + ne⁻ (Metal atoms lose electrons and enter the solution).
 
• At the **Cathode (Reduction)**: Mⁿ⁺ + ne⁻ → M (Metal ions gain electrons and deposit as pure metal).
 
 
 
• **Conductivity:** The electrolyte must have high **ionic conductivity** to ensure the process is energy efficient. The concentration of the **metal salt** and the **pH** of the solution are carefully maintained during industrial operations.
 
• **Purity Levels:** Electrolytic refining is capable of producing metals with a purity of up to **99.99%**, which is essential for electrical applications (like copper wiring) where impurities significantly increase resistance.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following fish production methods are done in the region of Kashmir?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aqua Culture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aqua Culture** is the primary method of fish production in the **Kashmir** region due to its vast **freshwater** resources, including rivers, lakes, and springs. It involves the breeding and harvesting of fish in controlled aquatic environments. ***Hence, the correct answer is Aqua Culture.***
 
• **Marine Fisheries** refer to fishing activities in oceans and seas. Since **Kashmir** is a **landlocked** mountainous region located far from any coastline, marine fishing is geographically impossible. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Brackish Water Fisheries** involve the farming of fish in water that has more salinity than fresh water but less than seawater, typically found in **estuaries** and **mangrove swamps**. The water bodies in **Kashmir** are predominantly fresh, lacking the salinity required for brackish water fish production. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pearl Culture** is the process of producing pearls by nurturing pearl oysters or freshwater mussels. While freshwater pearl culture exists in some parts of **India**, it is not a traditional or significant fish production method in the cold climatic conditions of the **Kashmir Valley**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Department of Fisheries** in **Jammu & Kashmir** focuses extensively on **Cold Water Fisheries**, leveraging the **oxygen-rich**, running waters of the Himalayas to boost the local economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Trout Farming:** **Kashmir** is globally renowned for its **Trout** production. Two main species are cultivated: **Brown Trout** (Salmo trutta fario) and **Rainbow Trout** (Oncorhynchus mykiss).
 
• **Historical Context:** **Trout** was first introduced to **Kashmir** by the **British** in the year **1900**. The first batch of **Trout ova** arrived from the **United Kingdom** as a gift to the then **Maharaja**.
 
• **Geographical Advantages:** The region possesses perennial water sources such as the **Jhelum River**, **Sindh River**, and high-altitude lakes like **Gangabal** and **Vishansar**, which maintain the low temperatures (below **20°C**) necessary for cold-water **Aqua Culture**.
 
• **Native Species:** Apart from exotic trout, the region is home to indigenous species known as **Schizothorax** (locally called **Kashir Gaad** or Snow Trout), which are well-adapted to the torrential mountain streams.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The fish industry in **Jammu & Kashmir** provides a livelihood to thousands of people, with major markets in **Srinagar** and exports to other parts of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kokernag Trout Farm:** Located in **Anantnag** district, it is considered **Asia's largest trout fishery** farm. It serves as a major hub for seed production and distribution.
 
• **Major Lakes:** **Wular Lake** and **Dal Lake** are significant centers for capture fisheries in the valley, contributing a large percentage of the total fish catch in the **Union Territory**.
 
• **Government Schemes:** The **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)** is being actively implemented in the region to modernize **Aqua Culture** infrastructure, including the construction of **RAS** (Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems) and cold storage facilities.
 
• **Blue Revolution:** The initiative to increase fish production in **Kashmir** is a part of the broader **Blue Revolution** in **India**, aimed at achieving self-sufficiency in protein sources and doubling farmers' income by **2024-25**.
</ul

questions.question: Fertilization in females usually occurs in which region of the reproductive system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fallopian Tube**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fertilization** is the biological process of the fusion of a **haploid male gamete (sperm)** and a **haploid female gamete (ovum)** to form a **diploid zygote**.
 
• In the human female reproductive system, the **location** where fertilization usually occurs is the **Fallopian tube**, also commonly referred to as the **oviduct**.
 
• Specifically, the fusion typically takes place in the **ampulla** region, which is the widest and longest part of the tube, or at the **ampullary-isthmic junction**.
 
• During **ovulation**, a mature **egg** is released from the **ovary** and is swept into the tube by the **fimbriae** (finger-like projections).
 
• The **sperm** must travel through the **vagina**, **cervix**, and **uterus** to reach the **Fallopian tube** to encounter the egg.
 
• The **ovum** remains viable for fertilization for approximately **12 to 24 hours** after being released.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ovary**:
 
 
• The **ovaries** are the primary **female sex organs** responsible for producing **ova** (eggs).
 
• They also secrete essential hormones such as **estrogen** and **progesterone** which regulate the **menstrual cycle**.
 
• In a typical **28-day cycle**, one egg is released from one of the two ovaries.
 
 
 
• **Uterus (Womb)**:
 
 
• The **uterus** is a hollow, pear-shaped **muscular organ** located in the **pelvic cavity**.
 
• Its primary **function** is to support the development of the **fetus** during **pregnancy**.
 
• The inner lining, called the **endometrium**, is where the **embryo** implants itself after traveling down from the tube.
 
 
 
• **Vagina**:
 
 
• The **vagina** is a muscular, elastic canal that serves as the **birth canal** during delivery.
 
• It acts as the **receptacle** for **sperm** during sexual intercourse and provides a pathway for **menstrual flow** to leave the body.
 
 
 
• **Fallopian Tube Structure**:
 
 
• There are two **Fallopian tubes**, each measuring about **10 to 12 cm** in length.
 
• They consist of four parts: the **infundibulum** (with fimbriae), the **ampulla**, the **isthmus**, and the **uterine part**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implantation**: After fertilization in the tube, the **zygote** undergoes **cleavage** (cell division) as it moves toward the **uterus**. It takes about **6 to 10 days** for the resulting **blastocyst** to attach to the **uterine wall**.

questions.question: Substitution reaction involves:

options.text: Addition of atoms to double bonded molecules
Replacement of a carbon atom with hydrogen
One atom or group of atoms being replaced by another
Removal of atoms to form simpler molecules

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One atom or group of atoms being replaced by another**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **substitution reaction** (also known as a single displacement reaction) is a chemical reaction during which a **functional group** or an **atom** in a chemical compound is replaced by another functional group or atom. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• These reactions are highly significant in **organic chemistry**. Saturated hydrocarbons, such as **alkanes**, primarily undergo substitution reactions because they contain **single covalent bonds** that are stable and do not allow for the addition of more atoms without removing existing ones.
 
• The process involves the **cleavage** of an existing **sigma bond** and the simultaneous or sequential **formation** of a new sigma bond with the substituting species.
 
• A common example is the **halogenation** of **methane (CH4)**. When methane reacts with **chlorine (Cl2)** in the presence of **ultraviolet light** or heat, one or more hydrogen atoms are replaced by chlorine atoms to form **chloromethane (CH3Cl)** and **hydrogen chloride (HCl)**.
 
• Unlike **addition reactions**, the saturation level of the molecule typically remains unchanged in a simple substitution reaction. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect*** as it describes addition reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Substitution Reactions:**
 
 
• **Nucleophilic Substitution:** This occurs when the "attacking" species is a **nucleophile** (an electron-rich species like **OH-** or **CN-**). It is common in **alkyl halides** and is further divided into **Sn1** (unimolecular) and **Sn2** (bimolecular) mechanisms based on the **reaction kinetics**.
 
• **Electrophilic Substitution:** This occurs when an **electrophile** (an electron-deficient species) displaces an atom. This is the characteristic reaction of **aromatic compounds** like **benzene**, where a hydrogen atom on the ring is replaced (e.g., **nitration** or **sulfonation**).
 
• **Radical Substitution:** This involves **free radicals** as intermediates. It usually requires **UV radiation** to initiate the process by breaking bonds **homolytically**, as seen in the **chlorination of alkanes**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other reaction types:**
 
 
• **Addition Reactions:** These involve atoms being added to **unsaturated** molecules containing **double or triple bonds** (alkenes or alkynes), resulting in a more saturated product.
 
• **Elimination Reactions:** These involve the **removal** of atoms or groups from a molecule, often resulting in the formation of **pi bonds** (double or triple bonds). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Replacement of Carbon:** Organic substitution reactions generally involve replacing **hydrogen** or a **functional group** attached to a carbon atom, rather than replacing the carbon atom itself. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leaving Group:** In a substitution reaction, the atom or group that is detached is called the **leaving group**. The efficiency of the reaction often depends on how stable the leaving group is after it departs.
 
• **Catalysts:** Many electrophilic aromatic substitutions require a **Lewis acid catalyst**, such as **FeCl3** or **AlCl3**, to generate a strong enough electrophile to attack the stable **benzene ring**.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Substitution reactions are used extensively in the **pharmaceutical industry**, the production of **polymers**, and the synthesis of **dyes** and **pesticides**.
 
• **Reactivity Series:** In inorganic chemistry, a **metal** higher in the **reactivity series** can substitute (displace) a metal lower in the series from its salt solution (e.g., **Zinc** replacing **Copper** in copper sulfate).
</ul

questions.question: Which trophic level represents maximum concentration of pesticides by biological magnification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tertiary Consumer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biological Magnification** (or **biomagnification**) refers to the process where the **concentration of toxic substances**, such as **pesticides** or heavy metals, increases progressively at each **successive trophic level** of a food chain.
 
• The **Tertiary Consumer** occupies the **highest trophic level** in the provided options. Because these organisms consume secondary consumers, they accumulate the total chemical load from all the lower levels combined. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Primary Consumers**, which are **herbivores**, occupy the **second trophic level**. They ingest pesticides directly from producers, but their body concentration is significantly lower than that of top predators. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Producers** (such as **green plants**) represent the **first trophic level**. They absorb **non-biodegradable** chemicals from the soil or water. While they are the entry point for toxins, they contain the **lowest concentration** compared to consumers. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Secondary Consumers** are **carnivores** that feed on primary consumers. While their toxin levels are higher than those of herbivores, they still possess a lower concentration than the **Tertiary Consumers** who prey upon them. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Biomagnified Substances:**
 
 
• To undergo biomagnification, a substance must be **long-lived** (persistent), **mobile**, **soluble in fats** (lipophilic), and **biologically active**.
 
• Examples include **DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane)**, **BHC**, and heavy metals like **mercury**, **arsenic**, and **cadmium**.
 
• Because these substances are **fat-soluble**, they are not excreted easily through urine and instead accumulate in the **adipose tissues** of organisms.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Apex Predators:**
 
 
• **Apex predators** at the **Tertiary Consumer** level often suffer from reproductive failure or population decline due to high toxic loads.
 
• In the **year 1962**, scientist **Rachel Carson** highlighted the dangers of **DDT** in her book **"Silent Spring,"** noting how it led to the **thinning of eggshells** in birds of prey like **eagles** and **falcons**.
 
• This phenomenon eventually led to a **ban on DDT** for agricultural use in many **countries**, including the **United States** in **1972**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The 10% Energy Law vs. Biomagnification:**
 
 
• According to **Raymond Lindeman's 10% Law** (proposed in **1942**), only about **10 percent** of **energy** is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
• While **energy decreases** as we go up the pyramid, the **concentration of non-biodegradable chemicals increases**. This inverse relationship is critical for understanding ecosystem health.
 
• **Bioaccumulation** occurs within a **single organism** over its lifetime, whereas **Biomagnification** occurs **across multiple trophic levels** in a food web.
 
 
 
• **Human Health Implications:**
 
 
• As **humans** often act as **Tertiary Consumers** (eating fish, poultry, or meat), they are highly susceptible to the effects of **biological magnification**.
 
• Consumption of **mercury-contaminated fish** led to the famous **Minamata disease** in **Japan** during the **1950s**, showcasing the lethal potential of high-trophic level toxin accumulation.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: When iron filings are mixed with sulfur powder and the mixture is heated, a black substance called iron sulfide is formed. Which statement best describes the changes involved?

options.text: A chemical change occurs as a new substance is formed.
A physical change occurs as the substances are only mixed.
A reversible physical change takes place.
Iron dissolves in sulfur forming a solution.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A chemical change occurs as a new substance is formed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **iron filings** and **sulfur powder** are simply mixed together at **room temperature**, they form a **heterogeneous mixture**. This is a **physical change** because no chemical bonds are broken or formed, and the **iron** retains its **magnetic properties**.
 
• When the mixture is **heated**, a **chemical reaction** occurs between the two elements to form a new compound called **Iron(II) sulfide (FeS)**. This substance is a **black solid** that has entirely different **chemical and physical properties** compared to the original reactants. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The formation of **Iron sulfide** is a **chemical change** because a **new substance** is created with a fixed **chemical composition**. Unlike the initial mixture, the components of the compound cannot be separated by simple **physical means** such as using a **magnet**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Chemical changes are generally **irreversible** by physical methods. Once **Iron sulfide** is formed, you cannot retrieve the **iron** and **sulfur** by cooling it or filtering it. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Iron does not **dissolve** in sulfur to form a solution; instead, the atoms undergo a **chemical bonding** process (ionic/covalent character) to form a **crystal lattice** of **FeS**. A solution is a **homogeneous mixture** where no chemical reaction occurs. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical vs. Physical Changes**: 
 
 
• A **physical change** alters the form of a substance but does not change its **molecular identity**. Examples include **melting**, **shredding**, or **mixing**.
 
• A **chemical change** results in the formation of **new chemical substances**. Signs of a chemical change include **color change**, **temperature change** (evolution of heat), and the formation of a **precipitate** or **gas**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Reactants**:
 
 
• **Iron (Fe)** is a **greyish-metallic** element that is **ferromagnetic**, meaning it is strongly attracted to magnets.
 
• **Sulfur (S)** is a **bright yellow** non-metal powder that is **insoluble in water** but soluble in solvents like **carbon disulfide (CS2)**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of the Product (Iron Sulfide)**:
 
 
• **Iron(II) sulfide** is a **non-magnetic** black solid. 
 
• It reacts with **dilute hydrochloric acid** to produce **hydrogen sulfide gas (H2S)**, which has a characteristic **rotten egg smell**, whereas the original mixture of Fe and S would produce **hydrogen gas** when reacted with acid.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exothermic Nature**: The reaction between **iron** and **sulfur** is **exothermic**, meaning it **releases energy** in the form of **heat** and **light** once the activation energy is provided by initial heating.
 
• **Law of Constant Proportions**: In the compound **Iron sulfide**, iron and sulfur are always present in a **fixed ratio by mass** (approximately **7:4**), regardless of how much of each was initially mixed.
 
• **Separation Techniques**: In the **mixture stage**, iron can be separated using a **magnet** and sulfur can be separated by **dissolving** it in **carbon disulfide**. These techniques fail once the **chemical change** into **FeS** has occurred.
</ul

questions.question: The kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving with a velocity v is 25 J. What will be its kinetic energy when its velocity is increased three times (3v) ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**225 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** is the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion**. It is defined as the work needed to accelerate a body of a given **mass** from rest to its stated **velocity**.
 
• The mathematical formula for Kinetic Energy is **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** represents the **mass** of the object and **v** represents its **velocity**.
 
• According to the question, the initial kinetic energy of the object with mass **m** and velocity **v** is **25 J**. Therefore, **1/2 mv² = 25 Joules**.
 
• When the **velocity is increased three times**, the new velocity becomes **3v**.
 
• Substituting the new velocity into the formula: New Kinetic Energy = **1/2 m(3v)²**. Since **(3v)² = 9v²**, the expression becomes **9 * (1/2 mv²)**.
 
• Given that the value of **1/2 mv²** is **25 J**, the new kinetic energy is calculated as **9 * 25 = 225 J**. ***Hence, the calculation shows the final kinetic energy is 225 J.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Relationship between Velocity and Energy:** Kinetic energy is **directly proportional to the square of the velocity**. This means that if the velocity doubles, the energy increases by **4 times** (2²), and if the velocity triples, the energy increases by **9 times** (3²).
 
• **SI Unit:** The standard unit of energy is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**. One Joule is equivalent to **1 kg.m²/s²**.
 
• **Mass Dependency:** Kinetic energy is also **linearly proportional to the mass** of the object. If the mass of the object is doubled while keeping the velocity constant, the kinetic energy will also **double**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Kinetic energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only magnitude and **no direction**. It is always a non-negative value (zero or positive) because mass is positive and the square of velocity is always positive.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This principle states that the **net work done** on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. This is a fundamental concept in **classical mechanics** used to solve various physics problems involving **force** and **displacement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Frame of Reference:** While the mass of an object is constant, its **velocity** (and thus its kinetic energy) depends on the **frame of reference** from which it is measured.
 
• **Types of Kinetic Energy:** In addition to **translational kinetic energy** (studied here), there is also **rotational kinetic energy** (1/2 Iw²) for spinning objects and **vibrational kinetic energy**.
 
• **Relativistic Effects:** At extremely high speeds approaching the **speed of light (c)**, the classical formula 1/2 mv² becomes inaccurate, and **Einstein's theory of special relativity** must be applied to calculate energy.
 
• **Conversion:** Kinetic energy can be converted into other forms of energy, such as **potential energy** (e.g., a ball thrown upwards) or **thermal energy** (e.g., through friction).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following acts as an olfactory indicator in acid-base reactions?

options.text: Onion extract changes smell in bases
Methyl orange produces odour in base

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Onion extract changes smell in bases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are substances whose **odour** or **smell** changes depending on whether they are mixed with an **acidic** or **basic** solution.
 
• **Onion extract** is a classic example of an olfactory indicator. When a basic solution like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** is added to onion extract, the characteristic **smell** of the onion **cannot be detected** or vanishes. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Turmeric** is a **natural indicator** that changes color in different media. It remains **yellow** in acidic solutions but turns **reddish-brown** in basic solutions. It does not turn blue. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is a **synthetic indicator**. It is **colorless** in **acidic** solutions and turns **pink** in **basic** solutions. The statement claims it turns pink in acids, which is factually wrong. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Methyl orange** is another **synthetic indicator** that shows a distinct color change. it turns **red** in **acidic** media and **yellow** in **basic** media. It is not an olfactory indicator and does not rely on producing or changing odour to indicate pH. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Onion extract changes smell in bases.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Olfactory Indicators:**
 
 
• **Vanilla Essence:** The pleasant smell of **vanilla** is retained in **acidic** solutions but is **destroyed** or lost when added to a **base**.
 
• **Clove Oil:** In **acidic** solutions, the smell of **clove oil** remains, but it changes or disappears in **basic** solutions.
 
• These indicators are particularly useful in **chemistry laboratories** for **visually impaired students**, as they can identify the nature of a substance through the sense of **smell** rather than sight.
 
 
 
• **Natural Indicators:**
 
 
• **Litmus:** Derived from **Lichens**, it is **purple** in neutral solutions, **red** in acids, and **blue** in bases.
 
• **China Rose (Gudhal):** It turns **dark pink (magenta)** in **acidic** solutions and **green** in **basic** solutions.
 
• **Red Cabbage Extract:** It remains **red** in acids but turns **green** or **yellow** in basic solutions.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:**
 
 
• These are **man-made** chemicals used to detect pH. Common examples include **Phenolphthalein** and **Methyl orange**.
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is often used in **acid-base titrations** because of its sharp color change at a **pH** range of approximately **8.2 to 10.0**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **pH Scale:** The acidity or basicity is measured on a **pH scale** ranging from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is **neutral** (like pure water), a **pH less than 7** is **acidic**, and a **pH greater than 7** is **basic**.
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:** When an **acid** and a **base** react, they form **salt and water**. Indicators are used to find the **equivalence point** of these reactions.
 
• **Chemical Nature of Olfactory Change:** The change in smell occurs because the **odorous molecules** (which are often weak acids themselves) react with the **hydroxide ions (OH-)** in a base to form **odorless salts**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following factors primarily determines the size of an atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of electrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **size of an atom** is primarily determined by the space occupied by its **electrons**. While the **nucleus** contains more than **99.9%** of the atom's mass, it occupies an insignificantly small volume compared to the total size of the atom.
 
• The **volume** of an atom is defined by the **electron cloud**, which is the region where **electrons** are likely to be found. As the **number of electrons** increases, they occupy more **energy levels** or **shells**, which significantly expands the **atomic radius**.
 
• The **atomic radius** is the distance from the center of the **nucleus** to the outermost stable **electron shell**. Therefore, the physical boundary that determines "size" is essentially the limit of the **electron distribution**. ***Hence, option 1 is the primary factor.***
 
• While the **number of protons** (atomic number) affects the pull on the electrons, and the **mass of the nucleus** and **number of neutrons** affect the weight and stability, they do not define the physical dimensions or volume of the atom in the same way **electrons** do. ***Hence, options 2, 3, and 4 are incorrect as primary determinants of size.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Radius Trends:**

 
 
• **Down a Group:** In the **Periodic Table**, the atomic size **increases** as you move down a **group**. This is because a **new electron shell** is added for each succeeding element, moving the outermost **electrons** further from the **nucleus**.
 
• **Across a Period:** Atomic size generally **decreases** from **left to right** across a **period**. This occurs because the **number of protons** increases, creating a stronger **positive charge** that pulls the **electron cloud** closer to the **nucleus**, despite the number of shells remaining the same.
 
 
 
• **The Nucleus vs. The Atom:**
 
 
• To visualize the scale, if an atom were expanded to the size of a **football stadium**, the **nucleus** would be about the size of a **small marble** placed at the center, while the **electrons** would define the outer perimeter of the stands.
 
• The **nucleus** consists of **protons** and **neutrons**, which are much heavier than **electrons**, but they are packed into an extremely dense, tiny area of roughly **10^-15 meters** in diameter.
 
 
 
• **Shielding Effect:**
 
 
• This is a phenomenon where **inner electrons** act as a shield, reducing the **attractive force** between the **positive nucleus** and the **outermost electrons**. This effect allows the **electron cloud** to expand, further influencing the overall **atomic size**.
 
 
 
• **Effective Nuclear Charge (Zeff):**
 
 
• This refers to the net **positive charge** experienced by an **electron** in a multi-electron atom. It is a crucial concept in **General Chemistry** that explains why atoms with more **protons** aren't always larger; the increased **Zeff** pulls the **electrons** inward, counteracting the size increase.

questions.question: Which of the following cell structures helps amoeba to acquire its food material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plasma membrane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amoeba** is a **unicellular eukaryotic organism** that does not have a fixed shape. It relies entirely on its **plasma membrane** (or cell membrane) to interact with its external environment.
 
• The process by which **Amoeba** acquires its food is known as **endocytosis**. This is possible because the **plasma membrane** is highly **flexible** and composed of **lipids and proteins**, allowing it to deform and engulf particles.
 
• To capture food, the **Amoeba** extends temporary, finger-like projections of the **plasma membrane** called **pseudopodia** (meaning "false feet"). These extensions surround the food particle until they fuse together.
 
• Once the **pseudopodia** fuse, the food particle is trapped inside a small, membrane-bound cavity within the cell called a **food vacuole**. This specific type of ingestion of solid matter is often referred to as **phagocytosis**.
 
• The **plasma membrane** serves as the primary interface for **nutrition**, as the organism lacks specialized mouth-like structures found in more complex multicellular animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plasma Membrane:**
 
 
• It is a **selectively permeable membrane** that regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• In addition to **food acquisition**, it provides **protection** to the internal cellular contents and maintains the cell's integrity.
 
 
 
• **Cilia:**
 
 
• These are short, hair-like structures found on the surface of some cells. In organisms like **Paramecium**, **cilia** help in movement and in pushing food into a specific "mouth" area called the **cytostome**. **Amoeba** does not possess **cilia**.
 
 
 
• **Flagella:**
 
 
• These are long, whip-like structures used primarily for **locomotion** in certain **bacteria** and **protists** like **Euglena**. While they can help create currents to move food, they are not the primary structure for food engulfment in **Amoeba**.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Membrane:**
 
 
• This is a double-layered membrane that surrounds the **nucleus** of a **eukaryotic cell**. Its function is to protect the **genetic material (DNA)** and regulate the flow of information between the **nucleus** and **cytoplasm**. It has no role in the external acquisition of food.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Digestion:** Once the food is inside the **food vacuole**, **digestive enzymes** from the **cytoplasm** are secreted into the vacuole to break down the food into simpler, diffusible nutrients.
 
• **Exocytosis:** After the nutrients are absorbed, the **undigested waste** is moved toward the **plasma membrane**. The membrane then ruptures at any point to expel the waste outside the body, a process known as **egestion**.
 
• **Habitat:** **Amoeba** are typically found in **freshwater** bodies like **ponds, lakes, and slow-moving rivers**, where they feed on **bacteria, algae, and other microscopic organisms**.
 
• **Discovery:** The **Amoeba** was first discovered by **August Johann Rösel von Rosenhof** in the year **1755**.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a similarity between chloroplast and Mitochondria?

options.text: Both posses their own DNA and 70S Ribosome.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both possess their own DNA and 70S Ribosome**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chloroplasts** and **Mitochondria** are both **semi-autonomous organelles** because they contain their own **genetic material** and protein-synthesizing machinery.
 
• **Statement 1:** Both perform photosynthesis. This statement is incorrect because **photosynthesis** is a process exclusive to **chloroplasts** (found in plants and algae). **Mitochondria** do not perform photosynthesis; they are involved in breaking down nutrients. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Both possess their own DNA and 70S Ribosome. Both organelles contain **extra-chromosomal DNA** (usually circular) and **70S ribosomes**, which are similar to those found in **prokaryotic cells**. This allows them to produce some of their own **enzymes** and **proteins**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 3:** Both perform respiration. While both are energy-transducing organelles, the process of **aerobic cellular respiration** (ATP production via the Krebs cycle and Electron Transport Chain) is the primary function of **mitochondria**. Chloroplasts are primarily for **carbon fixation**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement 4:** Both have chlorophyll. **Chlorophyll** is the green pigment essential for capturing light energy during photosynthesis and is located within the **thylakoids** of **chloroplasts**. **Mitochondria** do not contain chlorophyll. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Both possess their own DNA and 70S Ribosome.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Commonly referred to as the **"Powerhouse of the cell"**, they are found in almost all **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• Their main function is the synthesis of **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)** through **cellular respiration**.
 
• They have a **double-membrane** structure where the inner membrane is folded into **cristae** to increase surface area for **oxidative phosphorylation**.
 
 
 
• **Chloroplasts:**
 
 
• These are a type of **plastid** primarily found in the **mesophyll cells** of leaves in **green plants**.
 
• They contain **chlorophyll** and **carotenoid** pigments responsible for trapping light energy for **photosynthesis**.
 
• Like mitochondria, they are **double-membrane** bound and contain a fluid matrix called **stroma** and stacked sacs called **grana**.
 
 
 
• **The Endosymbiotic Theory:**
 
 
• This evolutionary theory, popularized by **Lynn Margulis** in the **1960s**, suggests that mitochondria and chloroplasts originated as free-living **prokaryotic organisms**.
 
• The presence of **70S ribosomes** and **circular DNA** inside these organelles is strong evidence of their **bacterial ancestry**, as eukaryotic cytoplasm typically contains **80S ribosomes**.
 
• Both organelles reproduce independently of the cell nucleus through a process similar to **binary fission**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Ribosomes:** In a eukaryotic cell, the **cytoplasmic ribosomes** are **80S** (composed of 60S and 40S subunits), whereas the **organellar ribosomes** (mitochondrial and plastidial) are **70S** (composed of 50S and 30S subunits).
 
• **DNA Type:** The **DNA** found in these organelles is typically **naked** (not associated with histone proteins) and **circular**, mirroring the structure of **plasmid DNA** in **bacteria**.
 
• **Energy Transformation:** While mitochondria convert **chemical energy** (glucose) into **metabolic energy** (ATP), chloroplasts convert **solar energy** into **chemical energy** (sugar).
</ul

questions.question: The molecular mass of a compound is 63 u. If it contains one hydrogen atom and three oxygen atoms, the atomic mass of the remaining element is :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **molecular mass** of a substance is the sum of the **atomic masses** of all the atoms in a molecule of that substance. It is therefore the relative mass of a molecule expressed in **atomic mass units (u)**.
 
• In the given problem, the total **molecular mass** of the compound is **63 u**. The compound consists of **one hydrogen atom**, **three oxygen atoms**, and one unknown element.
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Hydrogen (H)** is **1 u**. Since there is **one hydrogen atom**, its contribution to the total mass is **1 u**.
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Oxygen (O)** is **16 u**. Since the compound contains **three oxygen atoms**, their total contribution is calculated as **3 x 16 u = 48 u**.
 
• To find the **atomic mass** of the remaining element, we subtract the masses of the known components from the total **molecular mass**: **63 u - (1 u + 48 u) = 63 u - 49 u = 14 u**. ***Hence, the calculated mass is 14 u.***
 
• The element that possesses an **atomic mass** of **14 u** is **Nitrogen (N)**. Therefore, the compound is **Nitric Acid**, which has the chemical formula **HNO3**. ***Hence, the correct option is 14 u.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nitric Acid (HNO3)**:
 
 
• It is a **highly corrosive** mineral acid, also known as **aqua fortis** or the spirit of niter.
 
• In its pure form, it is colorless, but older samples tend to acquire a **yellow cast** due to decomposition into oxides of nitrogen and water.
 
• It is widely used in the manufacture of **fertilizers** (like ammonium nitrate), **explosives** (like TNT and nitroglycerin), and in **metal refining**.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u)**:
 
 
• The **atomic mass unit** is defined as a mass exactly equal to **one-twelfth (1/12th)** of the mass of one **carbon-12 atom**.
 
• The **unified atomic mass unit (u)** has replaced the older **amu** designation in modern scientific literature.
 
• It allows chemists to calculate **formula mass** and **molar mass**, facilitating the study of **stoichiometry** in chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of constituent elements**:
 
 
• **Hydrogen**: The lightest element in the periodic table with **atomic number 1**. It usually exists as a **diatomic gas (H2)**.
 
• **Oxygen**: A highly reactive **nonmetal** and oxidizing agent. It is the **third-most abundant element** in the universe by mass.
 
• **Nitrogen**: A colorless, odorless gas that makes up about **78%** of **Earth's atmosphere**. It is essential for life as a component of **amino acids** and **DNA**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Calculation Summary**:
 
 
• Total Mass: **63**
 
• Mass of H: **1**
 
• Mass of 3 O: **48** (3 x 16)
 
• Equation: **1 + X + 48 = 63**
 
• Result: **X = 14**
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other options**:
 
 
• **32 u** is the **atomic mass** of **Sulfur (S)**. If the element were sulfur, the molecular mass would have been **81 u** (HSO3 - hypothetical radical).
 
• **16 u** is the **atomic mass** of **Oxygen (O)**.
 
• **12 u** is the **atomic mass** of **Carbon (C)**. For a compound like **HCO3** (Bicarbonate), the mass would be **61 u**.
 
 
 
• **Date of Discovery**: **Nitric acid** was first synthesized by the alchemist **Jabir ibn Hayyan** around **800 AD**. Its composition was accurately determined by **Henry Cavendish** in **1785**.
</ul

questions.question: If a conductor has a potential difference of 1 volt across its ends and a current of 1 ampere flows through it, what is its resistance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 ohm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between **voltage**, **current**, and **resistance** in an electrical circuit is defined by **Ohm's Law**, which states that the **current** flowing through a conductor is **directly proportional** to the **potential difference** applied across its ends, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• Mathematically, **Ohm's Law** is expressed as **V = IR**, where **V** is the **potential difference**, **I** is the **current**, and **R** is the **resistance** of the conductor.
 
• In this specific problem, the given **potential difference (V)** is **1 volt** and the **electric current (I)** is **1 ampere**.
 
• To calculate the **resistance**, we use the formula **R = V / I**. Substituting the values: **R = 1 volt / 1 ampere**.
 
• The resulting calculation gives **R = 1 ohm**. This implies that **1 ohm** is the resistance of a conductor when a **potential difference** of **1 volt** results in a **current** of **1 ampere**. ***Hence, the correct option is 1 ohm.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Resistance (R)**:
 
 
• **Resistance** is the property of a conductor by virtue of which it opposes the flow of **electric current** through it.
 
• The **SI unit** of **resistance** is the **Ohm**, represented by the Greek symbol **Ω (omega)**.
 
• The value of **resistance** depends on the **length** of the conductor, its **area of cross-section**, the **nature of the material**, and the **temperature**.
 
 
 
• **Georg Simon Ohm**:
 
 
• The law and the unit of **resistance** are named after the **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm**, who published his findings in **1827**.
 
• His work was fundamental in the development of the theory of **electricity** and **circuits**.
 
 
 
• **Potential Difference (V)**:
 
 
• It is defined as the **work done** to move a **unit charge** from one point to another in an **electric field**. Its **SI unit** is the **Volt**.
 
• A device used to measure **potential difference** is called a **voltmeter**, which is always connected in **parallel** across the points where the **voltage** is to be measured.
 
 
 
• **Electric Current (I)**:
 
 
• It is the **rate of flow of electric charges** (usually **electrons**) through a conductor. The **SI unit** is the **Ampere**.
 
• An **ammeter** is used to measure **current** in a circuit and is always connected in **series**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ohmic and Non-Ohmic Conductors**:
 
 
• **Ohmic Conductors**: Materials that obey **Ohm's Law** (where **V** is proportional to **I**) are called **ohmic**. Examples include **copper**, **silver**, and **aluminum**. Their **V-I graph** is a **straight line**.
 
• **Non-Ohmic Conductors**: Devices that do not follow **Ohm's Law** are **non-ohmic**. Examples include **semiconductors**, **diodes**, **transistors**, and **vacuum tubes**.
 
 
 
• **Resistivity (ρ)**:
 
 
• While **resistance** changes with shape, **resistivity** is a **characteristic property** of the material. It is measured in **ohm-meter (Ωm)**.
 
• **Insulators** like **glass** and **rubber** have very high **resistivity** (**10^12 to 10^17 Ωm**), whereas **metals** have low **resistivity** (**10^-8 to 10^-6 Ωm**).
 
 
 
• **Effect of Temperature**:
 
 
• For **pure metals**, **resistance increases** with an **increase in temperature**. However, for **semiconductors** like **silicon** and **germanium**, **resistance decreases** as **temperature increases**.

questions.question: Which of the following changes can be regarded as part of sexual maturation in human males?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cracking of voice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sexual maturation** in human males is primarily driven by the onset of **puberty**, typically occurring between the ages of **11 and 16 years**.
 
• One of the most distinct physical changes is the **Cracking of voice**. This happens because the **Larynx** (voice box) grows significantly larger during this period. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• As the **Larynx** grows, it begins to protrude at the front of the neck, forming what is commonly known as the **Adam's apple**.
 
• During this transition, the **Vocal Cords** become longer and thicker. Before they fully adjust to the new size, the voice may "crack" or fluctuate between high and low pitches before settling into a deeper tone.
 
• While an **Increase in weight** and **Increase in height** occur during the adolescent growth spurt, they are general developmental changes seen in both sexes and are not exclusive indicators of male sexual maturation. ***Hence, statements 3 and 4 are not the most specific answers for sexual maturation.***
 
• **Deposition of fat in hips** is a secondary sexual characteristic typically associated with **female** maturation to facilitate childbirth. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Testosterone:** This is the primary **androgen** (male sex hormone) secreted by the **Testes**. It is responsible for the development of male **Secondary Sexual Characteristics** and the stimulation of **Spermatogenesis** (production of sperm).
 
• **Secondary Sexual Characteristics in Males:** These include the appearance of **facial hair** (mustache and beard), **pubic hair**, **axillary hair** (underarm), and the broadening of the **shoulders** and chest.
 
• **Pituitary Gland:** The process of maturation begins when the **Pituitary Gland** releases **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** and **Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)**, which signal the testes to produce testosterone.
 
• **Physical Composition:** Unlike females, who experience fat deposition in the pelvic region, males typically experience an increase in **Muscle Mass** and a decrease in body fat percentage relative to muscle during puberty.
 
• **Primary vs. Secondary Characteristics:** **Primary characteristics** are the reproductive organs themselves (testes, penis), while **Secondary characteristics** (like voice deepening) are the physical signs of sexual maturity that do not involve the reproductive tract directly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timing:** The onset of these changes can vary based on **Genetics**, **Nutrition**, and **Environmental factors**. In recent decades, studies have shown a slight trend toward earlier onset of puberty in some populations.
 
• **Growth Spurt:** The **Peak Height Velocity (PHV)** in boys usually occurs about **two years** later than in girls. During this time, bones grow rapidly, and the **Epiphyseal plates** eventually close, marking the end of height growth.
 
• **Skin Changes:** Increased activity of **Sebaceous Glands** (oil glands) often leads to **Acne** during the phase of sexual maturation due to hormonal fluctuations.
</ul
